title: 290. Functions, Graphs & Transformations: Horizontal Line Test
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for a Quadratic Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=x^2\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Consider the function \(f(x)=x^2\). Does its graph pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: A horizontal line such as \(y=1\) intersects the graph of \(y=x^2\) at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\). Since a horizontal line meets the graph in more than one point, the graph fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Check whether any horizontal line can meet the parabola in two different points.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for an Absolute Value Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=|x|\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(f(x)=|x|\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: The horizontal line \(y=1\) intersects the graph of \(y=|x|\) at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\). Since one horizontal line meets the graph twice, the graph fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Consider a horizontal line above the vertex of the V-shaped graph.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for a Linear Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=2x+3\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(f(x)=2x+3\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: The function \(f(x)=2x+3\) is a nonconstant linear function with slope \(2\), so it is strictly increasing. Every horizontal line intersects its graph exactly once. Therefore, the graph passes the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Use the slope of \(f(x)=2x+3\) to decide whether two different inputs can give the same output.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for a Quadratic Function with Two Zeros
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=x^2-4x\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(f(x)=x^2-4x\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: Consider the horizontal line \(y=0\). Solving \(x^2-4x=0\) gives \(x(x-4)=0\), so \(x=0\) or \(x=4\). Thus the horizontal line \(y=0\) intersects the graph at two points, so the graph fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Try the horizontal line \(y=0\) and solve for \(x\).

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test from a Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine from a table whether a function passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question:
The function \(f\) is defined by the table:
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & -1 & 0 & 1 & 2\\
\hline
f(x) & 3 & 1 & 3 & 5
\end{array}
\]
Does \(f\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: From the table, \(f(-1)=3\) and \(f(1)=3\). The horizontal line \(y=3\) intersects the graph at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\). Since one horizontal line meets the graph in more than one point, \(f\) fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Look for two different \(x\)-values that have the same output value.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test from Given Points
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a graph fails the horizontal line test from two points with the same \(y\)-coordinate.
questions.question: The graph of \(f\) passes through the points \((-2,5)\) and \((3,5)\). Does the graph pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: Both points have the same \(y\)-coordinate, \(5\). Therefore, the horizontal line \(y=5\) intersects the graph at \(x=-2\) and \(x=3\). Since one horizontal line meets the graph at more than one point, the graph fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: A single horizontal line through both points is enough to fail the test.

questions.concept: Consequence of Failing the Horizontal Line Test
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a function failing the horizontal line test can have an inverse without restricting its domain.
questions.question: If the graph of \(f\) fails the horizontal line test, can \(f\) have an inverse function without restricting its domain?
questions.explanation: Failing the horizontal line test means the function is not one-to-one: two different inputs give the same output. An inverse function requires the original function to be one-to-one; otherwise the inverse would not be a function. Therefore, \(f\) cannot have an inverse function without restricting its domain.
questions.hint: Recall the relationship between one-to-one functions and inverse functions.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for a Quartic Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=x^4\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(f(x)=x^4\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: The horizontal line \(y=1\) intersects the graph of \(y=x^4\) at \(x=-1\) and \(x=1\), since \((-1)^4=1\) and \(1^4=1\). Because one horizontal line meets the graph twice, the graph fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Even powers often give the same output for opposite inputs.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for a Cubic Function
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=x^3\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(f(x)=x^3\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation: The function \(f(x)=x^3\) is strictly increasing. For any real number \(y\), the equation \(x^3=y\) has exactly one real solution, \(x=\sqrt[3]{y}\). Therefore, every horizontal line intersects the graph at most once, so the graph passes the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Strictly increasing functions pass the horizontal line test.

questions.concept: Horizontal Line Test for a Quartic Function with Even Symmetry
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether \(f(x)=x^4-2x^2\) passes the horizontal line test.
questions.question: Does the graph of \(f(x)=x^4-2x^2\) pass the horizontal line test?
questions.explanation:
Evaluate \(f\) at opposite inputs:
\[
\begin{aligned}
f(1) &= 1^4-2(1)^2=1-2=-1\\
f(-1) &= (-1)^4-2(-1)^2=1-2=-1
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the horizontal line \(y=-1\) intersects the graph at \(x=1\) and \(x=-1\). Since one horizontal line meets the graph in more than one point, the graph fails the horizontal line test.
questions.hint: Check whether the function gives the same output for opposite input values.
